description:
SOUNDNESS-CRITICAL COMPARATOR SURFACE: this TODO's work lives in
benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py, which is covered by
.github/CODEOWNERS (`benchbox/core/equivalence/** @joeharris76`). Its PR will
require code-owner review before merge regardless of CI status - budget for
that review cycle, do not assume `make pr-open`'s normal auto-merge applies.

Verified by reading cross_surface.py on this branch:
`_READ_PRIMITIVES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` (lines 859-885) is a plain
`dict[str, str]` with 17 keys built from `dict.fromkeys(...)` over six waiver
classes:
  - approx_count_distinct_simple_expression/pandas,
    approx_count_distinct_groupby_expression/pandas,
    approx_quantile_groupby_expression/pandas (6 keys) -> `_READ_PRIMITIVES_APPROX`
    (HyperLogLog / T-Digest sketch error)
  - statistical_percentiles_expression/pandas (2 keys) ->
    `_READ_PRIMITIVES_DECIMAL_PERCENTILE` (DECIMAL(15,2) vs float64 percentile scale)
  - optimizer_common_subexpression_expression/pandas (2 keys) ->
    `_READ_PRIMITIVES_DECIMAL_ROUND` (DECIMAL vs float64 ROUND half-cent boundary)
  - min_by_complex_expression/pandas (2 keys) -> `_READ_PRIMITIVES_ARGMIN_TIE`
    (ARG_MIN tie-break non-determinism)
  - json_aggregates_expression/pandas (2 keys) -> `_READ_PRIMITIVES_JSON_TEXT`
    (JSON text vs native container representation)
  - map_access_expression, map_construction_expression,
    map_keys_values_expression (3 keys) -> `_READ_PRIMITIVES_POLARS_MAP`
    (Polars has no Map dtype)

A bare `str` value in `known_divergences` is documented at
`ClassifiedDivergence`'s own docstring (cross_surface.py:340-347) as tolerating
ANY divergence on that key - "which masks a real regression that happens to
land on the same query/backend". So today, if `approx_count_distinct_simple_pandas`
regressed from "close to the true count" to "wildly wrong" (e.g. a broken sketch
merge, an off-by-a-factor-of-1000 bug), the gate would stay green: the bare-string
waiver accepts the cell unconditionally.

The codebase already has the fix pattern, applied twice:
  - h2odb Q9 (cross_surface.py:785-816): `_h2odb_q9_decimal_residue` parses the
    value-mismatch detail, checks it is the p90 column, checks the SQL side is at
    DECIMAL(8,2) scale, and bounds `abs(orig - variant) <= _H2ODB_Q9_RESIDUE_MAX`.
  - clickbench Q18 (cross_surface.py:606-624+): `_is_clickbench_q18_arbitrary_topn`
    matches the divergence class ("Value mismatch") for the order-less top-N tie case.

Both wrap a `reason` string and an `accepts: Callable[[SurfaceDivergence], bool]`
in `ClassifiedDivergence` (cross_surface.py:338-357), which is a drop-in
replacement for a bare-string value in the same `known_divergences` dict - no
new plumbing is needed, only new predicate functions per waiver class.

This TODO converts all 17 Read Primitives keys to `ClassifiedDivergence` with a
class-appropriate bound, so an out-of-bounds divergence on any of these cells is
reported as an unclassified gate failure instead of silently passing.

anti_patterns.dont: fork ResultValidator or find_cross_surface_divergences to add this
anti_patterns.why: the existing known_divergences/ClassifiedDivergence mechanism already supports per-key predicates.

anti_patterns.dont: loosen a predicate until the CURRENT gate passes without checking the accepted value is still the SAME documented residue
anti_patterns.why: that reintroduces the exact vacuity this TODO fixes.

anti_patterns.dont: remove a waiver instead of classifying it merely because the current divergence looks small
anti_patterns.why: Read Primitives is a primitives benchmark that deliberately exercises engine features (sketches, approximate quantiles) with no exact DataFrame equivalent; some divergence is legitimate, it just needs a bound.

anti_patterns.dont: write one generic 'accept any numeric difference under X' predicate shared across unrelated waiver classes
anti_patterns.why: the sketch-error, DECIMAL-epsilon, and tie-membership bounds have different bases and conflating them hides which bound actually fired.

deferrals.reason: Out of scope for this TODO, which targets the 17 read_primitives keys identified by this review; a future gate should adopt ClassifiedDivergence from the start per this pattern, not require a follow-up conversion.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Reason states future gates should adopt ClassifiedDivergence from the start rather than needing a retrofit; no other gated benchmark flagged as needing conversion now.
deferrals.summary: Apply the same ClassifiedDivergence conversion to any bare-string waivers in other gated benchmarks beyond read_primitives (e.g. future additions to GATES).

preserves.behavior: No other gated benchmark's known_divergences or legitimately_empty entries are touched.
The read_primitives GATE stays in the enforced `GATES` registry (cross_surface.py) throughout; do not move it to STAGED_GATES to work around a broken predicate.

`make read-primitives-cross-surface-equivalence-report` stays green (currently: every compared cell matches or is classified) after every conversion - a converted waiver must still accept the CURRENT, legitimate divergence, only reject a wider one.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:338-357 ClassifiedDivergence - the dataclass to reuse for every converted waiver; do not invent a parallel mechanism.

benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:606-624 _is_clickbench_q18_arbitrary_topn / _CLICKBENCH_TIE_AMBIGUOUS - the divergence-class-matching predicate pattern (useful for the JSON-text and Map-dtype classes, which cannot be numerically bounded).
benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:785-816 _h2odb_q9_decimal_residue / _H2ODB_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES - the DECIMAL-scale-bounded predicate pattern to mirror for the percentile/round classes.

tests/integration/test_cross_surface_mutation_sensitivity.py - the existing mutation-probe harness (wraps a DataFrameQuery via dataclasses.replace, drives find_cross_surface_divergences + the real ResultValidator); extend its pattern per converted waiver class rather than building a new harness.

verifications.expected: exit 0; every previously-waived cell now reports under a named ClassifiedDivergence class, not a bare string

work_units.notes:
HyperLogLog / T-Digest have documented error bounds (HLL: ~2% relative
error at BenchBox's precision; T-Digest: small relative error near the
median, larger toward tails). Parse the value-mismatch detail (reuse the
`_VALUE_MISMATCH_RE` pattern from the h2odb predicate) and bound the
relative difference between the DuckDB approx value and the DataFrame
exact value to a documented multiple of the sketch's error bound - not an
arbitrary epsilon. Cite the bound's source (DuckDB HLL/T-Digest docs or a
measured empirical bound at this benchmark's cardinality) in the reason
string.

DONE. `_read_primitives_sketch_residue` (cross_surface.py) pins each of
the 3 sub-queries to its documented result column(s) via
`_READ_PRIMITIVES_SKETCH_COLUMNS` (grouping-key columns excluded) and
bounds relative error to `_READ_PRIMITIVES_SKETCH_RELATIVE_ERROR_MAX =
0.15`, derived from measured residues at this cell: simple 4.2-4.6%,
groupby 10.0-10.6%, quantile 3.8% - bound is ~1.4x the largest observed,
documented HLL (~2% nominal at 12-bit precision) as the theoretical basis
with the empirical measurement as the actual derivation (per-group
cardinality pushes the residue above the textbook figure). Gate stays
green; predicate rejects wrong-column and >15%-off values (unit-tested).
work_units.summary: Write and apply a sketch-error-bounded predicate for the approx_count_distinct_*/approx_quantile_* classes (6 keys)

work_units.notes:
Reuse `_is_two_decimal_scale` (cross_surface.py:770-782) to confirm the SQL
side is DECIMAL(15,2)-rounded, and bound `abs(orig - variant)` to a sub-cent
epsilon (mirror `_H2ODB_Q9_RESIDUE_MAX`'s derivation - document the epsilon's
basis, do not copy the h2odb constant blind). Two waiver classes, same shape
of predicate; write one helper parameterized by column index if the shapes
allow it, or two small predicates if the value positions differ.

DONE. One shared helper `_read_primitives_decimal_scale_residue(column,
max_residue)` parameterizes both: `_read_primitives_percentile_decimal_residue`
pins statistical_percentiles' p95 (column 6) to
`_READ_PRIMITIVES_PERCENTILE_RESIDUE_MAX = 0.005 + 1e-6` (half-cent, same
derivation as h2odb Q9 - measured residue 0.004);
`_read_primitives_round_decimal_residue` pins
optimizer_common_subexpression's rounded_revenue (also column 6) to
`_READ_PRIMITIVES_ROUND_RESIDUE_MAX = 0.01 + 1e-6` (a full cent - DuckDB

`_H2ODB_Q9_RESIDUE_MAX`, even where numerically identical.
work_units.summary: Write and apply a DECIMAL-scale epsilon predicate for statistical_percentiles_* and optimizer_common_subexpression_* (4 keys)

work_units.notes:
ARG_MIN ties: the predicate must confirm the value column (the price/metric
being minimized) matches exactly across surfaces and only the tie-broken
column (e.g. p_name) differs, AND that the differing value is genuinely a
member of the tied group (look up the tie set from the underlying data, or
bound the predicate to asserting the metric values are equal while the
picked names differ - never accept a divergence where the metric itself
differs).

DONE (bounded predicate variant, not full tie-set lookup). Projection is
[p_brand(0), cheapest_part_name(1), cheapest_part_type(2), min_price(3)];
`_read_primitives_argmin_tie` accepts a Value-mismatch ONLY on columns 1-2
(the two ARG_MIN outputs), rejecting the p_brand grouping key (0) and
min_price (3) - so the metric itself must always match. Documented the
SAME residual blind spot as h2odb Q9 (comparator reports only the first
positional mismatch per row, so a simultaneous min_price bug behind an
accepted name/type tie-break would not be visible) rather than silently
accepting a wider guarantee than is actually enforced.
work_units.summary: Write and apply a tie-membership predicate for min_by_complex_* (2 keys)

work_units.notes:
JSON_GROUP_ARRAY/OBJECT text vs native containers cannot be bounded
numerically. Write a predicate that parses both sides' JSON, confirms they
represent the SAME set/mapping of key-value pairs (order-insensitive,
number-format-insensitive), and rejects any divergence where the parsed
structures actually differ (a missing key, an added element, a wrong
value) - i.e. convert this from "match this label" to "match this
structural equality after parsing," not merely narrow the string.

DONE, with a finding beyond the TODO's original framing: the two gated
cells diverge in DIFFERENT shapes, verified via a diagnostic probe of the
built cell (both backends return the SAME 25 TPC-H p_brand values as the
SQL reference - not a missing/extra group):
  * json_aggregates_pandas is the anticipated "Value mismatch" (JSON text
    vs native list/dict) - `_read_primitives_json_equivalent` parses both
    sides (json.loads, falling back to ast.literal_eval) and compares
    structurally (order-insensitive lists, number-format-insensitive
    values via round(...,2)); a missing/added/wrong element compares
    unequal and is rejected.
  * json_aggregates_expression is instead an "ORDER BY key mismatch" -
    the Polars expression aggregate does not sort its groups. Accepted
    ONLY when both reported keys are members of TPC-H's fixed 25-value
    p_brand domain (`_READ_PRIMITIVES_BRAND_DOMAIN`), so an out-of-domain
    key (a genuinely wrong group) is still rejected. This is a narrower,
    more defensible bound than "any ORDER BY key mismatch on this key."
work_units.summary: Write and apply a text-shape predicate for json_aggregates_* (2 keys)

Confirm whether these three keys ever reach `known_divergences` lookup at

document why they are still declared, rather than inventing a synthetic
